newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil eyes more overseas refining deals.
newsitem.headline: Statoil eyes more overseas refining deals.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday processing agreements with foreign refineries had risen by around 30 percent and had opened new commercial opportunities for its trading and supply arm.
About 240,000 barrels of the two million barrels of crude Statoil trades daily are refined in its own refineries.

Karl Brekke in Statoil's processing unit said the percentage of crude refined outside of Norway probably will increase if the company goes ahead with plans to extend processing deals to the Asia-Pacific region.
Statoil said the main aim is to enhance the value of crude by converting it to gasoline and other products abroad and to market them instead of oil.

"In that way we can exploit Statoil's physical presence in all parts of the world and apply our expertise in refining and trading to building new commercial activity," Brekke told the company's Status Weekly newsletter.
Brekke declined to reveal the difference in profit between products and crude. He said output from the Heidrun field in the Norwegian Sea and from the North Sea Oseberg development was preferred.
Statoil said growing Asia-Pacific demand for products such as gasoline had fuelled its interest in processing deals in the region.

The company already has deals with Saras in Sardinia, Italy, Crown in the Gulf of Mexico and the Irish National Petroleum Co in Cork. Products from these agreements are mainly sold in the Mediterranean and in the United States.
